key_insight: The paper documents and critiques a rising trend of suspicion toward generative-AI use in academic manuscripts, showing that inconsistent policies and detection practices are creating harms (false positives, delays, and chilling effects) for researchers rather than clear safeguards.
problem_solved: Addresses the problem of how academic publishing is reacting to suspected generative-AI usage — specifically the absence of consistent, evidence-based policies and the resulting risks to fairness, reproducibility, and researcher trust.
method: Qualitative review of recent cases and editorial actions where generative-AI suspicion influenced publication outcomes
Analysis and comparison of journal policies and detection practices related to AI-assisted writing
Critical discussion synthesizing ethical, practical, and policy implications and proposing clearer community guidance
impact: Highlights urgent need for transparent, standardized policies and reliable practices so editors, reviewers, and authors can distinguish legitimate AI assistance from misconduct without unfairly penalizing researchers.
visual_elements: Timeline of notable editorial actions and policy announcements showing the rise in AI-suspicion incidents
Flowchart of the manuscript lifecycle highlighting decision points where AI-suspicion can cause delays or rejections
Comparison table or heatmap of journal policies (permissive → restrictive) and common detection methods
Icon-driven infographic showing consequences (false positives, delays, reputation risk) and recommended fixes (transparency, standardized disclosure, robust detection validation)
paper_title: On the troubling rise of generative AI suspicion in academic publishing
